questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Rohan and I am (1)/ best friends and (2)/ we often meet each other. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 i.e 1**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] ****Explanation**

**Looking at sentence we find that:**

 
• The error lies in **part 1 **of the sentence.
 
• Here the verb **am **is used after 'Rohan and I' which is incorrect. 
 
• Since 'Rohan and I' are two subjects i.e plural we should replace '**am'** with '**are'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] **Point to note**

 
• **The verb am is always used only with 'I**' alone.

Hence from the above points, we find that the error lies in part 1 of the sentence.

Thus, the correct sentence will be: 'Rohan and I **are** best friends and we often meet each other.'

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Hardly had he left (1)/ the stadium than it began (2)/ to rain heavily. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2 i.e 2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] ****Explanation**

**Looking at the sentence we find that**:

 
• The error lies in **part 2 **of the sentence. 
 
• The word **than** is wrong here as it is contextually wrong.
 
• The word **when** should be used here as it gives proper meaning to the sentence. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] **Point to note**

 
• **'Than' **is a word that denotes comparison, in the above sentence it is contextually wrong. 
 
• '**When**' is a word that denotes time, i.e after which, during or at. Thus it is the correct word to replace **than**.

Hence from the above points, we find that the error lies in **part 2 **of the sentence. 

Thus, the final sentence will be: 'Hardly had he left the stadium **when** it began to rain heavily.'

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Our company not only manufactures (1)/ plastic containers but (2)/ also steel containers. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 i.e 1**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] ****Explanation**

**Looking at the given sentence we find that:**

 
• The error lies in **part 1 **of the sentence. 
 
• The error is in the use of the **correlatives. **i.e **not only**.
 
• Here **not only **should be placed after manufactures. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] **Point to note**

**​****When using correlatives: **

 
• The rule is that all words that refer to both alternatives must** be placed before the first correlative. **
 
• Therefore the correlative here should come after the word **manufactures. **

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c57b654ce2734797ce027c29e531287c9d5f43773c26b6f728bf7cc28ca9c21c.png] ****Example**

 
• *He **not only** cheated his friends but also his parents. * [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0adb088d1a3935f82783cdb88a916e587d0813a932753e58333ab47915094baf.png] 
 
• *He cheated **not only** his friends but also his parents. * [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c971210a37d22e3eb8c77c43452e397bde2cc529bd6d93edeaa971e8f5a5e93b.png] 

Hence from the above points, we find that the error lies in the 1st part of the sentence hence **Option 1 **is the correct answer. 

Thus, the correct sentence will be: 'Our company manufactures **not only **plastic containers but also steel containers.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Her son has done and (1)/ is still doing excellent (2)/ work for his business. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically and contextually correct.
 
• In a compound sentence, both the **auxiliary verbs** and **main verbs **should be mentioned separately if they differ in number, form or voice.
 
• For example:
 
 
• Dexter has not and will not fail in the near future. (incorrect)
 
• Dexter has not **failed **and will not** fail** in the near future. (correct) (Here, the form of “fail” is different. One is “failed” and the other one is “fail”)
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, 'done' and 'doing' are two different forms of verb. Hence, they should be mentioned separately.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **4) No error**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• However, if the number, form and voice don’t differ, the auxiliary verb and main verb shouldn’t be mentioned separately.
 
 
• For example: I did not and will not go there. (correct) (Students might mistakably put “go” after “did not”. But the form, voice or number doesn’t differ. So, “go” will be omitted.)

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Although Rahul ran very (1)/ fastly he could not (2)/ catch the moving bus. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2 i.e 2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] ****Explanation**

**Looking at the above sentence we find that**:

 
• The error lies in **part 2 **of the sentence.
 
• The given word **fastly **is wrong as there is **no such word.**
 
• The correct word that should be used here is **fast**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] Point to note**

 
• The word **fast **in itself is an adjective and an adverb.
 
• So adding **ly **does not create an adverb or adjective but instead a **wrong word. **

**​**Hence from the above points, we find that the error lies in part 2 of the sentence due to the non-existing word fastly.

Thus the correct statement will be: 'Although Rahul ran very **fast** he could not catch the moving bus.'

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Contiguous
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Inaccessible**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Contiguous**" refers to things that are touching or sharing a common border or boundary. Therefore, the opposite of "**contiguous**" would be something that is not touching or sharing a common border or boundary.
 
• "**Inaccessible**" is the word that fits this description, as it means **something that is not easily reached or approached.**
 
• Example sentence using "**contiguous**":
 
 
• *The two countries had **contiguous **borders and shared many cultural and economic ties.*
 
 
 
• Example sentence using "**inaccessible**":
 
 
• *The peak of the mountain was **inaccessible **due to the rough terrain and dangerous conditions.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 4) inaccessible.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's have a look at the **meaning **of other words in options:-

 
 
• "**Adjacent**" means next to or adjoining something else. It is a synonym of "contiguous" and, therefore, not an antonym.
 
• "**Abutting**" means bordering or adjoining something else. It is also a synonym of "contiguous" and, therefore, not an antonym.
 
• "**Bitterness**" means having a harsh and disagreeable taste, or a feeling of resentment or hostility. It is not related to the meaning of "contiguous" and, therefore, not an antonym.

The word ‘proportions’ means ‘a part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole’ and conveys the proper meaning here. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: found in other ______ such as bitumen
questions.solution: The word ‘relations’ means ‘associations’ and does not fit here. The word ‘forms’ means ‘ the visible ***shape*** or configuration of something, a particular way in which a thing exists or appears’ and fits here correctly. The other words do not fit here. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the suitable title for the passage.

options.text: India's belief in policy of peace

questions.solution: The passage states how India believes in peace and has always practised it. It focuses on how India sticks to peace and the birth of the peaceful approach in India centuries ago. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT with respect to the given passage?

options.text: India's foreign policy is based on principle of peaceful non existence.
Gautam Buddha gave the message of Ahimsa.
Emperor Ashoka adopted the Buddhist creed of non-violence.
The message of Mahavira was the same as that of Gautam Buddha.

questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘*Ever since India achieved independence from British rule, she has followed an independent foreign policy which is based on the principle of **peaceful co-existence**.’ *Thus option 1 is incorrect. The other options are correct statements.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT with respect to India's approach towards peace?

options.text: It is a legacy of her centuries – old tradition and cultural heritage.
It is ingrained in traditional outlook – both philosophical and historical.
Buddha, Mahavira, Gandhi – all presented policy of peaceful – co-existence here.
India is an independent sovereign nation and should go away with the policy of peace.

questions.solution: It is not mentioned in the passage that India should do away with peace. ‘*And now that India is an independent, sovereign nation, it is but natural that she should preserve her previous freedom by following the same principles of thought and action that have brought her a status of dignity and that have been the soul of her past tradition and history.’ *Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, who among the following is termed as a 'Messiah '?
questions.solution:
It is mentioned in the passage 'In our own age,' there walked in flesh and blood a Messiah called Mahatma Gandhi, who showed the world the way of peace and non-violence.

Thus Mahatma Gandhi was termed as 'Messiah.' Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: For which of the following reason India is being respected for as a nation?
questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage 'India has for centuries been respected as a nation that believes in the policy of peace.' Thus it is clearly stated that India has been respected in the world due to its policy of peace. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.
